description: A tawny, dark-striped big cat with two long curved sabre canines, crouched and stalking forward through dry grass under a heavy grey sky. Dead branches and stubble fill the foreground. No text, no border or frame, and no visible wounds. The painted style and fur suggest a prehistoric predator.
reason: The animal reads as a striped, placental sabre-tooth cat in the Smilodon mould, not clearly a pouched marsupial. The scene asks for a low, cat-like marsupial with bony chin flanges protecting the canines, and neither the flanges nor any marsupial feature is visible. The artist should check whether this could be mistaken for a different sabre-tooth, or redraw with a more marsupial, lower-slung build.
